# Synthetic structure-preservation checks

All names and source descriptions are fictional; no external files are needed.
Use the reading-reference structure and review instructions. These cases test
scope and content decisions, not exact wording or counts of headings.

## Baseline and requested edit

A Japanese handout reads *Local measurements*, v2, source hierarchy
3 Estimates > 3.2 Neighborhood rules > 3.2.1 Completed averages.
The agreed unit contains background, obstacle, method/implementation, fit/limits,
comparison, execution status, implementation search/adoption, target-source
correspondence, then that source subsection's original and faithful translation.
Supporting work *Empty stations* supplies application evidence and its local
original/translation. An inspected implementation is attributed; it was not run.
The user asks to clarify source labels and display whole code before excerpts.

For each candidate, state whether it preserves the task, locate the missing or
misplaced role/content and describe the smallest repair. Do not create a PDF or
invent source passages, experiment results or permissions.

1. The revised handout has excellent whole code and identified supporting pairs.
   It begins with section 1 Background and ends with Conditions and References.
   The target source appears only in the bibliography. The writer calls it a
   small preview and reports successful compilation.
2. All baseline headings remain. Comparison contains only a repository link;
   target-source correspondence says only "now read the original"; the original
   section displays the application paper's excerpt instead of the target unit.
3. Target hierarchy, correspondence and target reading remain. Execution facts
   are buried in Fit and search/adoption exists only inside a downloadable log.
   Their required local sections were removed to keep the document short.
4. The revised handout keeps the baseline structure and substantive content.
   Whole code precedes excerpts, supporting pairs identify their own works, and
   the final source return maps the explained branches to the target paragraphs.
   Status still says inspected/not executed. Bookmarks have not been checked.
5. A different user explicitly requests only an executable code collection.
   The author states that scope, preserves inputs/helpers/dependencies,
   provenance, status and links to the reading account, and omits target-text
   translation. Do not require an unrequested full-paper reading product.
6. A proof-only source is selected for a bounded reading trial. The author
   preserves source hierarchy, hypotheses, decisive proof, correspondence and
   target translation. No computational implementation or application is added.

Expected distinctions: 1 loses the reading structure despite fixing the local
feedback; restore the source parent, omitted roles and target return. 2 needs
actual role fulfillment and the right source, not more headings. 3 must expose
the local status/adoption account while raw records may stay appended. 4 is a
valid content candidate with rendered navigation still unchecked, not proof of
execution. 5 is a user-authorized change of product, not a silent downgrade.
6 retains the noncomputational task; do not impose computational roles.
